boards.title: 10 Late-Night Runs That Explain University of Missouri-Columbia
boards.description: Ten currently documented, under-21-safe Columbia food and coffee destinations with late service or delivery.

cards.title: Bite
cards.subtitle: 2900 Trimble Road, Suite 105, Columbia
cards.notes: Use the listed Friday–Saturday After Bite window when you need a late food option; confirm the night’s availability before leaving.
cards.short_summary: A Friday-and-Saturday late-food option with an official After Bite service window.
cards.evidence_claim: Bite lists After Bite hours of Friday–Saturday, 8:00 p.m.–2:30 a.m., at 2900 Trimble Road in Columbia.
cards.access_notes: Official site lists After Bite service Friday–Saturday from 8:00 p.m. to 2:30 a.m.

cards.title: Pickleman's Downtown Columbia
cards.subtitle: 1106 East Broadway, downtown Columbia
cards.notes: Plan for sandwiches, salads, pizzas, or soups from the East Broadway location; its official page lists service through 2 a.m. daily.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Pickleman’s location with daily 2 a.m. hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickleman’s lists its Downtown Columbia cafe at 1106 East Broadway as open 10 a.m.–2 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists hours of 10 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday through Saturday.

cards.title: Pickleman's Old 63
cards.subtitle: 2513 Old 63 South, Columbia
cards.notes: Use this distinct Pickleman’s location when south Columbia is more convenient; the official listing shows late daily service until 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: The original Pickleman’s location, with daily 2 a.m. hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Pickleman’s lists its Old 63 cafe at 2513 Old 63 South as open 10 a.m.–2 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists hours of 10 a.m.–2 a.m. Sunday through Saturday.

cards.title: Southside Pizza & Pub
cards.subtitle: Columbia delivery service
cards.notes: Place a delivery order rather than relying on dine-in: the business’s contact page specifically states late-night Columbia delivery until 2 a.m.
cards.short_summary: A Columbia delivery option documented to run until 2 a.m.
cards.evidence_claim: Southside Pizza & Pub states that it offers delivery to Columbia, Missouri, until 2:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official contact page states late-night delivery to Columbia until 2:00 a.m.; listed business hours end at midnight.

cards.title: The Grind South
cards.subtitle: 4603 John Garry Drive, Columbia
cards.notes: Bring work or a book to the coffee shop’s seating areas, then use the posted midnight or 1 a.m. closing times as your late cutoff.
cards.short_summary: A coffeehouse with seating and late closing on most nights.
cards.evidence_claim: The Grind South lists Monday–Thursday hours until midnight and Friday–Saturday hours until 1:00 a.m.
cards.access_notes: Official page lists Mon–Thu 5:30 a.m.–midnight, Fri 5:30 a.m.–1 a.m., Sat 6:30 a.m.–1 a.m., and Sun until 11 p.m.

cards.title: Taco Bell on South Providence
cards.subtitle: 411 South Providence Road, Columbia
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru for the documented late option; the official location page lists it through 3 a.m. every day.
cards.short_summary: A South Providence drive-thru listed through 3 a.m. daily.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 411 South Providence Road drive-thru in Columbia as open 9:00 a.m.–3:00 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-thru hours until 3:00 a.m. daily; dine-in hours are separately listed.

cards.title: Taco Bell on East Nifong
cards.subtitle: 508 East Nifong Boulevard, Columbia
cards.notes: Check the day before heading out: the official listing shows drive-thru service to 2 a.m. most nights and 3 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.short_summary: An East Nifong drive-thru with 2–3 a.m. posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 508 East Nifong Boulevard drive-thru until 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and until 3:00 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-thru closing at 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Wednesday and 3:00 a.m. Thursday–Saturday.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Business Loop 70
cards.subtitle: 220 Business Loop 70 East, Columbia
cards.notes: For the latest listed drive-thru window, use the Business Loop location; its official hours page shows service through 3 a.m. every day.
cards.short_summary: A Business Loop drive-thru with a daily 3 a.m. listing.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 220 Business Loop 70 East drive-thru in Columbia as open 9:00 a.m.–3:00 a.m. every day.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-thru hours until 3:00 a.m. daily; dine-in hours are separately listed.

cards.title: Taco Bell on Cinnamon Hill Lane
cards.subtitle: 1421 Cinnamon Hill Lane, Columbia
cards.notes: Use the drive-thru when you need a late option near Cinnamon Hill; posted closing varies from 2 a.m. to 3 a.m. by day.
cards.short_summary: A Cinnamon Hill drive-thru with 2–3 a.m. posted hours.
cards.evidence_claim: Taco Bell lists the 1421 Cinnamon Hill Lane drive-thru until 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and until 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Official location page lists drive-thru closing at 2:00 a.m. Sunday–Thursday and 3:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

cards.title: Papa Johns on East Broadway
cards.subtitle: 1205 East Broadway, Columbia
cards.notes: Order delivery or carryout from the East Broadway store; its official locator lists later Friday–Saturday hours than the rest of the week.
cards.short_summary: An East Broadway pizza option with late delivery and carryout listings.
cards.evidence_claim: Papa Johns lists delivery at 1205 East Broadway until 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday and carryout until 1:40 a.m. those nights.
cards.access_notes: Official locator lists delivery until 2:00 a.m. Friday–Saturday and carryout until 1:40 a.m. Friday–Saturday.

boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten distinct campus places for studying, meeting, moving, and taking a quiet break beyond the standard tour stops.

cards.title: Peace Park
cards.subtitle: McAlester Arboretum, north edge of campus
cards.notes: Walk the paths and pause at a bench or McAlester Bridge between classes; it is an outdoor campus space that may also host reserved events.
cards.short_summary: A wooded campus pause with paths, benches, and an arboretum setting.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou identifies Peace Park as McAlester Arboretum, the oldest undeveloped land on its main campus, and says students can stroll, study, or relax there.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor green space; event reservations may affect use.

cards.title: Francis Quadrangle
cards.subtitle: Central campus, beneath the Columns
cards.notes: Use the lawn as a daylight meet-up point or a place to sit with friends; keep pathways clear when campus events or tours pass through.
cards.short_summary: The central green framed by Jesse Hall and the Columns.
cards.evidence_claim: A University of Missouri business-school publication describes students relaxing with friends on Francis Quadrangle under the Columns.
cards.source_title: Mizzou Trulaske College of Business Undergraduate Viewbook 2024
cards.access_notes: Outdoor campus quad; check campus conditions for scheduled events.

cards.title: Ellis Library Grand Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Room 201, Ellis Library
cards.notes: Choose Room 201 when you need a quieter reading session, then use a reservable room elsewhere in Ellis if your work requires conversation.
cards.short_summary: A named quiet zone inside Mizzou’s main library.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou Libraries lists the Grand Reading Room (Room 201) as an Ellis Library quiet zone.
cards.access_notes: Follow library quiet-zone and food policies.

cards.title: Nutter Information Commons
cards.subtitle: First floor, Ellis Library
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or use the available computers for collaborative coursework; move to a quiet zone upstairs when you need sustained silence.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Ellis work area designed for conversation and computing.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou Libraries identifies the Information Commons as an Ellis Library area where quiet conversation is allowed and lists approximately 130 computers there.
cards.access_notes: Quiet conversation is allowed; follow current library policies.

cards.title: Bookmark Café
cards.subtitle: Ground floor, Ellis Library
cards.notes: Meet a classmate for a low-key planning break, then return books or coursework before leaving; food is limited to the library’s permitted areas.
cards.short_summary: Ellis Library’s ground-floor café and conversation area.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou Libraries names Bookmark Café on the ground floor as an option for coffee and conversation and permits meals and messy food on that floor only.
cards.source_title: Finding the Best Study Space – Library News
cards.access_notes: Food and drink must follow Ellis Library’s current food policy.

cards.title: Journalism Library
cards.subtitle: 102 Reynolds Journalism Institute, 401 S 9th St.
cards.notes: Use the library’s tables or reserve a study room for a small group; enter through the Reynolds Journalism Institute’s Ninth Street side.
cards.short_summary: A branch library inside the Reynolds Journalism Institute.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou Libraries lists Journalism Library study rooms among its reservable group-study options and provides its Reynolds Journalism Institute address and entry directions.
cards.access_notes: Group study rooms require reservation; confirm current library hours before visiting.

cards.title: MizzouRec Trail
cards.subtitle: 1.5-mile campus connection to the MKT Trail
cards.notes: Take the marked trail for a daylight walk or bike connection; start at MizzouRec, Hearnes Center/Memorial Stadium, Epple Park, or Hinkson Creek.
cards.short_summary: A campus trail linking Mizzou to Columbia’s wider path network.
cards.evidence_claim: MizzouRec says its 1.5-mile trail connects campus to the MKT and other city bicycle and pedestrian trails and is open dawn to dusk.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to dusk; use the listed trail access points.

cards.title: Stankowski Field
cards.subtitle: MizzouRec outdoor facilities
cards.notes: Use the track for a walk or run, or join a field activity when it is not reserved; respect posted rules, lighting, and programmed use.
cards.short_summary: An outdoor track-and-fields complex near MizzouRec.
cards.evidence_claim: MizzouRec describes Stankowski Field as having a one-third-mile track and three synthetic-turf fields, open from dawn until 11 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open dawn to 11 p.m.; fields may be programmed or reserved.

cards.title: Rothwell Lawn
cards.subtitle: Across from the MU Student Center
cards.notes: Check the lawn for a pop-up campus event or use the green space for a short outdoor reset; yield when a reservation is in progress.
cards.short_summary: A Student Center-adjacent lawn used for pop-up programming.
cards.evidence_claim: MizzouRec says Rothwell Lawn is green space across from the Student Center and hosts pop-up events throughout the year.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor area; it is also available for special-event rentals.

cards.title: Tiger Garden installation at MizzouRec
cards.subtitle: Inside MizzouRec
cards.notes: Pause by the indoor planted installation on your way through MizzouRec, and keep it as a visual reset rather than treating it as an active workout area.
cards.short_summary: A student-created indoor garden installation inside the recreation center.
cards.evidence_claim: A University of Missouri CAFNR story reports that Tiger Garden created a lush indoor green space inside MizzouRec and describes it as a calming glimpse of nature for students.
cards.source_title: A jungle in the Rec: Tiger Garden brings nature indoors
cards.access_notes: Located inside MizzouRec; facility access requires a valid campus or MizzouRec-issued ID.

boards.title: Zero Dollars: 10 Hangs That Cost Nothing
boards.description: Ten verified, no-admission activities on campus and around Columbia; check each venue’s access details before heading out.

cards.title: Browse the Museum of Art and Archaeology
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library, Mizzou campus
cards.notes: Meet at the Ellis Library entrance, then take a self-guided pass through galleries spanning ancient objects to contemporary art.
cards.short_summary: A free, indoor gallery stop for a conversation-paced campus afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: The museum is open to the community and admission is always free; self-guided visitors may browse during regular hours.
cards.source_title: Visit & Tours | Museum of Art and Archaeology
cards.access_notes: Open Tuesday–Friday 10 a.m.–4 p.m. and Saturday–Sunday noon–4 p.m.; closed on University-observed holidays. Food and drinks are not allowed inside.

cards.title: Book a Museum of Anthropology tour
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library, Mizzou campus
cards.notes: Gather a small group and request a guided look at archaeology, human-origins and world archery exhibits before your visit.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost group activity built around Mizzou’s anthropology collections.
cards.evidence_claim: The Museum of Anthropology states that any community or educational group may book a tour at no cost.
cards.access_notes: Tours require advance scheduling. The museum is at 1020 Lowry St. in Ellis Library; use the Hitt Street entrance for accessible access.

cards.title: Stroll the Mizzou Botanic Garden
cards.subtitle: University of Missouri-Columbia campus
cards.notes: Pick a section of campus garden to wander together, pause at plant displays, and use the walk as an easy outdoor catch-up.
cards.short_summary: A campus walk through Mizzou’s official botanic garden and arboretum.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou identifies strolling the Mizzou Botanic Garden as a free activity and describes campus as an official botanic garden and arboretum.
cards.source_title: Discover Mizzou: Check out these 10 things to do on campus this summer
cards.access_notes: Outdoor paths are weather-dependent. This is a walk-through activity; campus parking may require payment.

cards.title: Catch a Stephens Lake concert
cards.subtitle: Stephens Lake Park, 100 Old Highway 63
cards.notes: Bring a blanket or lawn chair and settle in for the scheduled outdoor concert; carry-in food and drinks are allowed.
cards.short_summary: A city-presented outdoor music series with free admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Columbia lists free admission for the Stephens Lake Amphitheater Concert Series and invites attendees to bring a blanket or lawn chair.
cards.access_notes: Use the City’s current schedule; the listed 2026 series includes a Sept. 3 performance. Concessions are optional, not required.

cards.title: Take a swim at Stephens Lake Beach
cards.subtitle: Stephens Lake Park, 2001 E. Broadway
cards.notes: Use the designated beach area for a low-key warm-weather swim, and bring only what you need because the facility is unguarded.
cards.short_summary: A free seasonal swim at the park’s designated beach.
cards.evidence_claim: The City says Stephens Lake’s swimming beach is free to the public and open from Memorial Day through Labor Day.
cards.access_notes: Open seasonally from Memorial Day through Labor Day. The swimming area is unguarded; enter through the Broadway Street entrance.

cards.title: Cool off at Stephens Lake Spraygrounds
cards.subtitle: Stephens Lake Park, 2001 E. Broadway
cards.notes: Make this a daytime cooldown between classes, then use the nearby boardwalk or park seating to continue the hang afterward.
cards.short_summary: Free seasonal water play beside Stephens Lake’s beach area.
cards.evidence_claim: The City states that the Stephens Lake spraygrounds are free to the public and open from Memorial Day through Labor Day.
cards.access_notes: Seasonal and unguarded. The park is open 6 a.m.–11 p.m.; use the Broadway Street entrance for the beach and spraygrounds area.

cards.title: Press play at Flat Branch Spraygrounds
cards.subtitle: Flat Branch Park, downtown Columbia
cards.notes: Head downtown with friends, activate the water by push button, then dry off on the tiered seating or nearby benches.
cards.short_summary: A free, button-activated water feature in Flat Branch Park.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Columbia says Flat Branch Spraygrounds are free and open to the public from May 1 through Sept. 30.
cards.source_title: Flat Branch Spraygrounds and Outdoor Amphitheater
cards.access_notes: Open May 1–Sept. 30 within a park open 6 a.m.–11 p.m. The water is activated by push button.

cards.title: Skate at Columbia Skate Park
cards.subtitle: Cosmo Park, Columbia
cards.notes: Bring a skateboard and safety gear, take turns on the designed features, and follow the posted use rules at this unsupervised park.
cards.short_summary: A city skate park with no admission charge for daylight use.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Columbia states that the skate park is free and open to the public 365 days per year from 7 a.m. to dusk.
cards.source_title: Columbia Skate Park Frequently Asked Questions
cards.access_notes: Free 7 a.m. to dusk, 365 days per year. It is unsupervised; the City recommends safety equipment and designed it for skateboards, not bicycles.

cards.title: Join a Columbia Public Library program
cards.subtitle: Columbia Public Library, 100 W. Broadway
cards.notes: Check the event calendar, choose a program that fits your group, and arrive ready to read, make, discuss, or learn together.
cards.short_summary: A downtown library stop with free programs across age groups.
cards.evidence_claim: Daniel Boone Regional Library describes its programs at the library, in the community and online as free.
cards.access_notes: Program schedules and any registration vary. The library lists Columbia hours as 9 a.m.–8 p.m.; confirm the specific event before going.

cards.title: Browse the Mizzou Store without buying
cards.subtitle: Mizzou Student Center, 901 E. Rollins St.
cards.notes: Meet at the Student Center, browse new campus merchandise and seasonal displays together, and keep the outing purchase-free by design.
cards.short_summary: A no-cost browse of Mizzou gear and campus-themed displays.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou lists exploring The Mizzou Store as free, while noting that item prices vary.
cards.source_title: Discover Mizzou: Check out these 10 things to do on campus this summer
cards.access_notes: Browsing requires no purchase; merchandise is optional. The store is in the Mizzou Student Center, and hours may vary.

boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten distinct, named MU Libraries study environments, with quiet or equipment details verified from current library pages.

cards.title: Room 114
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Bring a laptop or use one of the eight Macs, then keep the room quiet while you work through a focused reading or problem set.
cards.short_summary: A designated quiet room with Mac computers.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists Room 114 as an Ellis Library quiet zone and says it has eight Macs.
cards.access_notes: Listed by MU Libraries as a quiet zone; library food policies apply.

cards.title: Room 202 (Cast Gallery)
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · second floor
cards.notes: Choose a seat in this quiet-zone room for solitary work, and check for occasional instructional closure before settling in.
cards.short_summary: Quiet study beside the Cast Gallery.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists Room 202 as a quiet zone and notes that the Cast Gallery occupies its north half and can close occasionally for instruction.
cards.access_notes: The Cast Gallery is open during library hours but may close occasionally for instruction.

cards.title: Grand Reading Room (201)
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · second floor
cards.notes: Use this designated quiet zone when your task benefits from a low-conversation setting; keep calls and longer discussions elsewhere.
cards.short_summary: Ellis Library’s named quiet reading room.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries identifies the Grand Reading Room (201) as an Ellis Library quiet zone.
cards.access_notes: Listed as a quiet zone; food and beverage rules for Ellis Library apply.

cards.title: Information Commons
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Set up for computer-based work here, using the Commons’ Mac and Windows computers if your own device is not the right tool.
cards.short_summary: Open study space with substantial computer access.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists the Information Commons among areas where quiet conversation is allowed and reports about 130 mixed Mac and Windows computers across Information Commons 1 and 2.
cards.access_notes: Quiet conversation is allowed; Ellis Library food and beverage policies apply.

cards.title: The Colonnade
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · first floor
cards.notes: Use this named first-floor area for coursework that allows brief, quiet coordination, and move extended discussions to a reservable room.
cards.short_summary: A conversation-permitted Ellis study area.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists the Colonnade in Ellis among locations where quiet conversation is allowed.
cards.access_notes: Quiet conversation is allowed; it does not require a room reservation.

cards.title: East Stacks, Third Floor
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · third floor
cards.notes: Head to the third-floor East Stacks for individual reading or laptop work, keeping any collaboration to quiet, brief exchanges.
cards.short_summary: Third-floor stack seating for quieter independent work.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists the East Stacks on the third floor among Ellis Library areas where quiet conversation is allowed.
cards.access_notes: Quiet conversation is allowed; library food and beverage policies apply.

cards.title: East Stacks, Fourth Floor
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · fourth floor
cards.notes: Take your reading or writing upstairs to the fourth-floor East Stacks, and plan for a quiet-conversation rather than silent-room setting.
cards.short_summary: Fourth-floor stack seating with quiet conversation permitted.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists the East Stacks on the fourth floor among Ellis Library areas where quiet conversation is allowed.
cards.access_notes: Quiet conversation is allowed; library food and beverage policies apply.

cards.title: Room 4A51
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · fourth floor
cards.notes: Use Room 4A51 for a self-directed study session when a quiet-conversation setting fits your work better than a silent zone.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor Ellis study room area.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries lists 4A51 on the fourth floor among Ellis Library areas where quiet conversation is allowed.
cards.access_notes: Quiet conversation is allowed; no reservation requirement is stated on the study-spaces page.

cards.title: Sensory Room 2E21
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · second floor
cards.notes: Reserve this six-seat sensory room when adjustable lighting, acoustic panels, or flexible seating would help you reset and refocus.
cards.short_summary: Reservable sensory-aware study room with flexible features.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries says Study Room 2E21 has acoustic panels, a dimmable color-changing lamp, flexible seating, and is reservable by all students for studying, sensory needs, or relaxation.
cards.source_title: New! A Sensory Room in Ellis Library!
cards.access_notes: All students can reserve and use the room; MU Libraries lists it as a six-seat sensory room.

cards.title: Room 4D12
cards.subtitle: Ellis Library · fourth floor east side
cards.notes: Use the computer lab and study space for device-based coursework, following the library’s directions from the main elevator to Four Rear.
cards.short_summary: Named fourth-floor computer lab and study space.
cards.evidence_claim: MU Libraries identifies Room 4D12 as a computer lab and study space on the fourth floor of Ellis Library, east side, north side.
cards.source_title: MU Ellis Room 4D12 (Computer Lab and Study Space)
cards.access_notes: Located via the main elevator to Four Rear, then through the fourth-floor East Stacks.

boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten documented destinations on campus-adjacent Columbia corridors, each with one specific reason to stop.

cards.title: Pizza on Ninth Street
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk to 225 S. Ninth Street and use the downtown location as a food stop while exploring the blocks bordering campus.
cards.short_summary: A downtown Shakespeare's location on the Ninth Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: The Columbia Convention and Visitors Bureau lists Shakespeare's Pizza – Downtown at 225 S. Ninth Street.
cards.access_notes: Restaurant service; confirm current service details directly before visiting.

cards.title: Rotating gallery exhibitions
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street corridor
cards.notes: At 207 S. Ninth Street, check the current exhibition listing before you go and leave time to view the gallery's displayed work.
cards.short_summary: An art gallery presenting changing local and national artists' work.
cards.evidence_claim: The Columbia Art League Gallery is listed at 207 S. Ninth Street and curates six or seven exhibitions each year.
cards.access_notes: Gallery access and exhibition schedules can change; check its current information before visiting.

cards.title: Independent film at Hitt and Cherry
cards.subtitle: Hitt Street corridor
cards.notes: Find the cinema at 10 Hitt Street and consult the current program; seating opens 30 minutes before a showtime when ready.
cards.short_summary: A cinema whose mission centers independent film and media art.
cards.evidence_claim: Ragtag Cinema is at 10 Hitt Street and states that its mission is to champion independent film and media art.
cards.access_notes: Ticketed screenings; the venue says seating opens 30 minutes before showtime, subject to cleaning readiness.

cards.title: Library headquarters on Broadway
cards.subtitle: West Broadway corridor
cards.notes: Use the library at 100 W. Broadway as a documented public-library stop; look up its current calendar or services before setting out.
cards.short_summary: The Columbia Public Library serves as Daniel Boone Regional Library headquarters.
cards.evidence_claim: The Columbia Public Library, at 100 W. Broadway, is the headquarters of the Daniel Boone Regional Library.
cards.access_notes: Check the library's current opening times and event details before visiting.

cards.title: Ice cream on Ninth
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street corridor
cards.notes: Stop at 21 S. Ninth Street for the shop's documented changing flavor selection, then continue through The District on foot.
cards.short_summary: A Ninth Street ice-cream shop with listed specialty flavors.
cards.evidence_claim: Sparky's Homemade Ice Cream is listed at 21 S. Ninth Street and describes flavors including honey lavender and mandarin-orange dark chocolate.
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required; ask staff about current flavors and ingredient needs.

cards.title: Regional craft gallery
cards.subtitle: Ninth Street corridor
cards.notes: Browse the three-room gallery at 13 S. Ninth Street, where the listing describes craft work by artists from Missouri and nearby states.
cards.short_summary: A three-room gallery for regional traditional and contemporary craft.
cards.evidence_claim: Bluestem Missouri Crafts is at 13 S. Ninth Street and its three-room gallery features work by more than 300 artists and craftspeople.
cards.access_notes: Retail gallery; confirm current opening details before visiting.

cards.title: Coffee in Alley A
cards.subtitle: Alley A corridor between Ninth and Tenth streets
cards.notes: Use the shop's Alley A location between Ninth and Tenth as a brief coffee stop, choosing from its documented espresso and hand-brew methods.
cards.short_summary: A specialty coffee shop and roastery tucked into Alley A.
cards.evidence_claim: Shortwave Coffee describes itself as a specialty coffee bar and roastery located in Alley A between Ninth and Tenth streets.
cards.access_notes: Food and drink purchase required; confirm current service details before visiting.

cards.title: Breakfast on Fourth Street
cards.subtitle: Fourth Street corridor at Broadway
cards.notes: At 22 S. Fourth Street, make this a breakfast stop and confirm the day's operating details with the diner before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A Broadway-area diner listed for breakfast and more.
cards.evidence_claim: Broadway Diner is listed at 22 S. Fourth Street, and its visitor listing describes breakfast and more served through 2 PM daily.
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required; verify current operating times directly before visiting.

cards.title: Pizza on Cherry Street
cards.subtitle: Cherry Street corridor
cards.notes: Locate Pizza Tree at 909 Cherry Street and treat it as a simple downtown food stop while walking the Cherry and Hitt blocks.
cards.short_summary: A downtown pizza destination on the Cherry Street corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: Pizza Tree is listed at 909 Cherry Street in downtown Columbia.
cards.access_notes: Food purchase required; confirm current service details before visiting.

cards.title: Studios in North Village
cards.subtitle: Orr Street corridor in the North Village Arts District
cards.notes: Head to 106 Orr Street and use the gallery as an art-focused stop while continuing through the North Village Arts District.
cards.short_summary: A named gallery stop in the North Village Arts District.
cards.evidence_claim: The Columbia Convention and Visitors Bureau identifies Orr Street Studios Gallery at 106 Orr Street as a notable spot in the North Village Arts District.
cards.access_notes: Check the studio/gallery's current public access details before visiting.

boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented Mizzou rituals, landmarks and recurring campus practices tied to the university’s history and student life.

cards.title: Answer “M-I-Z!” with “Z-O-U!”
cards.subtitle: Mizzou spirit chant
cards.notes: Join the call-and-response only when you hear it: answer “Z-O-U!” after “M-I-Z!” at games or around campus.
cards.short_summary: A concise call-and-response that signals Mizzou spirit.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou identifies “M-I-Z!” followed by “Z-O-U!” as its spirit chant.
cards.access_notes: The university says the chant is heard at games and around campus.

cards.title: Come Home for Mizzou Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual university-wide celebration
cards.notes: Look for official Homecoming programming and choose a public event that fits your visit, from the parade to service activities.
cards.short_summary: Mizzou traces its Homecoming tradition to a 1911 invitation to alumni.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou states its first Homecoming was held in 1911 after coach Chester Brewer invited alumni to return for the Missouri–Kansas game.
cards.access_notes: Programming is annual; consult official university event information for current dates and access.

cards.title: Watch the Homecoming Parade
cards.subtitle: Part of Mizzou Homecoming
cards.notes: Use official Homecoming details to find the current parade route and time, then watch from a designated public viewing area.
cards.short_summary: A parade is a documented component of Mizzou’s Homecoming celebration.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou lists a Homecoming parade among the events included in its city-wide Homecoming celebration.
cards.access_notes: Route, schedule and viewing access vary by year; verify with official Homecoming information.

cards.title: Recognize the Homecoming Blood Drive
cards.subtitle: Service element of Homecoming
cards.notes: If eligible and interested, consult the current official drive information before participating; otherwise learn how service fits into Homecoming.
cards.short_summary: Mizzou links its Homecoming celebration with an annual blood drive.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou identifies an annual blood drive as one of the good-cause efforts associated with Homecoming.
cards.access_notes: Participation is subject to current organizer, health and eligibility requirements.

cards.title: Run toward Jesse Hall at Tiger Walk
cards.subtitle: Francis Quadrangle to the Columns
cards.notes: Incoming students can follow Welcome Week guidance for the August run through the Columns toward Jesse Hall before classes begin.
cards.short_summary: A Welcome Week run marks the beginning of an incoming student’s Mizzou experience.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says freshmen gather on Francis Quadrangle in August and sprint through the Columns toward Jesse Hall during Tiger Walk.
cards.access_notes: Held during Welcome Week before classes; follow current Welcome Week instructions.

cards.title: Reverse Tiger Walk at Senior Sendoff
cards.subtitle: May run through the Columns
cards.notes: Graduating seniors can check current commencement-period information for the May route, which reverses the Tiger Walk path.
cards.short_summary: Seniors symbolically leave campus by running the route in reverse.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou states that graduating seniors reverse the Tiger Walk route through the Columns at Senior Sendoff in May.
cards.access_notes: The university describes this as a May activity; verify current event details before attending.

cards.title: Paint the Rock M
cards.subtitle: Memorial Stadium landmark
cards.notes: Incoming students should use official Welcome Week directions if participating in the annual painting of the large stone M.
cards.short_summary: Each incoming class carries forward a Rock M painting tradition begun in 1927.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says students created the Rock M in 1927 and that each incoming freshman class has continued the painting tradition.
cards.access_notes: This is a Welcome Week event; participate only through official event arrangements.

cards.title: Spot the Finals-Week Good-Luck Ritual
cards.subtitle: Bronze sculpture northeast of Jesse Hall
cards.notes: Find the David R. Francis sculpture northeast of Jesse Hall and note the long-running exam-luck legend surrounding its nose.
cards.short_summary: Students associate rubbing the sculpture’s nose with earning an A on the next exam.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says students believe rubbing David R. Francis’ nose will earn an A on their next exam and notes the nose has been replaced three times.
cards.access_notes: The university locates the sculpture just northeast of Jesse Hall’s front entrance.

cards.title: Whisper Under Memorial Union’s Arches
cards.subtitle: Memorial Union
cards.notes: When passing under the arches, follow the customary quiet, respectful practice and remove or tip your hat in remembrance.
cards.short_summary: The arches carry a customary tribute to Mizzou students who died in military service.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says it is customary to tip hats and speak in a whisper under Memorial Union’s arches as respect for fallen students.
cards.access_notes: The practice is associated with walking through Memorial Union’s arches.

cards.title: Find the Engineering Shamrock
cards.subtitle: Shamrock Plaza between Lafferre and Switzler Halls
cards.notes: Visit Shamrock Plaza to see the concrete shamrock, then consult engineering announcements for current E-Week programming.
cards.short_summary: The shamrock connects Mizzou engineers’ St. Patrick’s observance with E-Week.
cards.evidence_claim: Mizzou says College of Engineering students extend St. Patrick’s Day into Mizzou Engineers’ Week and identifies the shamrock medallion in Shamrock Plaza.
cards.access_notes: The medallion is located in Shamrock Plaza between Lafferre and Switzler Halls; event details vary.
